title: Bathroom Where Ran Collapsed As Well
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shinichi Kudo, Kogoro Mouri, Inspector) omitted by convention, but Ran Mouri and Masumi Sera are included as full person nodes because this episode makes them structurally load-bearing: Ran is a secondary victim of the chloroform trap (she collapses in the bathroom exactly as Rumi was meant to), and Sera delivers the case's central red herring (a wrong, fully-argued deduction that Rumi Kitao staged Waka's corpse and killed her), which Shinichi then dismantles point-by-point over the phone. The old lower-fidelity case file's stated culprit (Kenya Settsu, s2) and its core clues (planted fingerprints, poor eyesight, missing contact lens) all check out against the transcript -- no culprit-swap needed here, unlike some other rebuilds. What the old file missed/flattened: (1) Sera's full false-accusation-of-Rumi arc, a major red-herring set piece, was omitted entirely; (2) the real motive was specific -- Waka was blackmailing Kenya, threatening to expose his past mistreatment of other girls to the chairman's daughter he was courting for social advancement, not generic 'jealousy amid an adultery investigation' (that jealousy angle was Rumi's, and it was the false theory's motive, not Kenya's real one); (3) the coin-handoff behavioral test and the old photo showing all four friends in glasses (now all wearing contacts) were both omitted, though they are the clues that actually let Conan pin the crime on Kenya specifically over Kaga; (4) several present-but-unlisted named people (Ran, Sera, Keiko Kitao, the unnamed chairman's daughter) are added here. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The corpse's lipstick was removed but mascara still trickled from the eye -- a culprit who thought to remove lipstick for the face pack but missed mascara is almost certainly male, contradicting the theory that a woman staged the scene.

When Conan held out his hand for dropped coins, Kaga placed them directly into his palm, but Kenya put them into his own palm and held it out instead -- the same fumble he made handing Rumi the spare key, revealing poor depth perception unique to Kenya among the suspects.

An old photo shows all four friends wearing glasses about two years ago, but none of them wear glasses now -- establishing they all switched to contacts, which is what makes a missing/found contact lens meaningful evidence.

Kenya is missing one contact lens; a matching lens, with his fingerprints, is found hidden inside Waka's eye, where she concealed it as she lost consciousness -- placing him at the moment of the attack.
